headline: Fixed-fee contracts with the majors shield SkyWest from the fuel shock: it grew EPS while peers cut guidance, yet trades at 5.3x EBITDA.
business: The largest U.S. regional airline (522 regional jets in service or under contract), flying as United Express, Delta Connection, American Eagle and Alaska. Most flying is under capacity-purchase agreements (CPAs) where the major partner pays a fixed fee and bears fuel cost.
recent: Q3 2026 diluted EPS of $3.08, up from $2.81 a year earlier, on revenue of $1.12B (reported Oct 29).
Higher fuel prices hurt only the smaller prorate (revenue-sharing) segment, where SkyWest does bear fuel.
Repurchased $75M of stock in Q3 with ~$238M of authorization left; 69 more E175s are scheduled for delivery, mostly to partner contracts.
strengths: Business model largely passes fuel cost to partners
Cheapest stock in the group: EV/EBITDA 5.3x, forward P/E 7.6x
risks: Concentrated customers: pressured majors could cut regional flying
Prorate segment does carry fuel risk
Pilot supply and contract renewal terms
catalysts: Q4 results and placement of 33 still-unassigned E175 deliveries
Re-rating as the market recognizes fuel insulation
